chunks: Hamzah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alavi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim informed me, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them), saying:

Seven [types of people] are not to have the Quran recited to them [or do not recite the Quran]: the bowing one, the prostrating one, one in the toilet, one in the bath, the one in major ritual impurity, the woman in childbed, and the menstruating woman.

The author of this book (may God be pleased with him) said: This indicates detestation (karahah), not absolute prohibition (nahy). This is because for the one in major ritual impurity and the menstruating woman, reciting the Quran is generally permissible, except for the four obligatory prostrations: Surah Luqman, Ha-Mim al-Sajdah, An-Najm when it runs, and Surah Iqra (Al-'Alaq). It has also been narrated that a man may recite the Quran in the bath provided his recitation is not vocalized loudly, as long as he is wearing a waistcloth. As for bowing and prostrating, one does not recite in them because the primary act in them is glorification, except what has been narrated regarding the Prayer of Need. As for the toilet, it is obligatory to keep the Quran from being recited in it. As for the woman in childbed, she follows the ruling of the menstruating woman in this regard.

key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: The one in major ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: What are the seven conditions under which reciting the Quran is considered disliked in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq categorizes these seven states as makruh (detested) rather than mandub (prohibited), distinguishing between physical impurity (junub, hadith, postpartum) and ritual postures (ruku, sujud) where the primary dhikr is glorification. He notes that while general recitation is permissible in the bath if not vocalized, the toilet requires greater reverence to preserve the Quran's sanctity, whereas the four specific surahs containing obligatory prostrations allow for recitation despite the state of impurity.
